name: Post/Page Edit Restriction Days
author: Josef Namin

sections.description:
Many companies or website owners are concerned about editors or other users inadvertently or intentionally editing or removing posts after they have been published. The Post/Page Edit Restriction Days plugin helps you restrict post or page edits after a specific number of hours or days once they are published.

For example, you can set a restriction of 3 days, after which only admin or authorized roles can edit the post or page. This prevents unauthorized or accidental changes to content after it’s been live for a set period.

Features

  • Restrict post/page edits after a set number of days.
  • Control which user roles can edit posts or pages after the restriction period.
  • Simple and easy-to-use plugin for content control.
  • Prevent unwanted changes from editors or contributors.

Translations

We welcome volunteers to help translate the plugin into other languages! Please visit the WordPress Translate Project to help us.
sections.installation:
1. Via WordPress Admin Panel:

    • Go to your WordPress Admin Dashboard.
    • Navigate to Plugins > Add New.
    • Search for “Post/Page Edit Restriction Days”.
    • Click Install Now and then Activate the plugin.

  2. Manual Installation:

    • Download the plugin zip file.
    • Upload the Post/Page Edit Restriction Days folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
    • Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
sections.faq:
How do I use the “Day Restriction” feature?

After installing the plugin, go to the Post or Page section of your WordPress dashboard. You’ll see a new “Day Restriction” button that allows you to set how many days a post can remain editable. After the specified period, only admins or authorized roles will be able to make changes.

I have another question, who can I contact?

For support, feel free to email us at: [itadminjn@jobbid.org]
